channel.title: Tak Wing Yu | Physiotherapy Educator and Researcher
channel.description: I explore how emerging technologies can support critical thinking, experiential learning, and practice readiness in health professions education—without replacing the human judgement at the centre of clinical care.

item.title: When Teaching Becomes Boring: Do Educators Need Novelty Too?
item.description: A reflection on repetition, professional curiosity and why experienced educators may sometimes need to become novices again.

item.title: Should We Assess Students With AI — or Without It?
item.description: A two-lane approach reframes AI assessment around purpose: support learning with contemporary tools, then assure independent clinical capability where it matters.

item.title: A Conference Should Change What Happens on Monday
item.description: A reflection on turning conference conversations and notes into sharper questions, small commitments and observable changes in teaching and research.

item.title: What a Guest Lecturer Adds That a Slide Cannot
item.description: Guest expertise becomes educational when it is connected to curriculum outcomes, active student participation and purposeful follow-up.

item.title: What Group Work Makes Visible Before Assessment
item.description: Group activity can reveal developing reasoning, participation patterns and misconceptions before formal assessment makes them difficult to address.

item.title: Beyond a Score: What Content-Mastery Quizzes Make Visible
item.description: Content-mastery quizzes can reveal useful patterns in learning and teaching, but a score is evidence to interpret rather than proof of clinical competence.

item.title: A Simulation Room Is Only the Beginning
item.description: Realistic facilities create possibilities, but simulation becomes educational through purposeful outcomes, participation, facilitation and debriefing.

item.title: A VR Demonstration Is Not Yet a Learning Experience
item.description: A headset demonstration can attract attention, but purposeful learning requires a clear problem, active participation, reflection and aligned evidence.

item.title: Why Universities Are Attracted to VR, and Why Novelty Is Not Enough
item.description: Virtual reality attracts attention through immersion, visualisation and novelty, but meaningful adoption begins with a learning problem and a sustainable implementation plan.

item.title: The Clinical Education Triangle: Students, Clinical Educators and Visiting Lecturers
item.description: A placement visit prompted me to reflect on how students, clinical educators and visiting lecturers can turn three partial perspectives into a useful feedback loop.

item.title: Practising What We Teach: Staying Connected to Clinical Practice
item.description: Experiencing a cervical traction setup from the other side of the treatment table reminded me why educators should remain curious, clinically connected and attentive to the learner and patient experience.

item.title: Beyond the Right Answer: Why We Should Ask Students to Explain
item.description: Why a correct performance is not enough when the reasoning remains hidden—and how focused explanation can strengthen physiotherapy assessment.

item.title: When AI Can Read but Cannot Act: Why a Limitation May Be a Safeguard
item.description: A real calendar task prompted me to reconsider whether an AI assistant's refusal is a failure—or a useful boundary around permission, privacy and accountability.

item.title: AI Integration Needs a Theory of Learning
item.description: Six design principles for asking whether AI strengthens professional learning—or merely improves the artefact.

item.title: Should I Use AI for This? From Personal Choice to Health CARE‑AI
item.description: A practical bridge from deciding whether to use AI for a task to making its use contextual, accountable, responsible and equitable in health professions education.

item.title: The Next AI Problem Is AI Authenticity Fatigue
item.description: What happens when genuine human writing is treated as AI-generated before anyone has read it closely?

item.title: From Classroom to Clinic: What Is Healthcare's Equivalent of TRAIN?
item.description: Competence matters, but readiness also depends on judgement, adaptation, entrustment and support.

item.title: The Clinician Is Not the Only Learner: What Role Rotation Might Add to Simulation
item.description: A cautious reflection on how learner, peer patient, observer and peer debriefer roles may support different aspects of learning—and what further studies still need to confirm.

item.title: Lecturers Need AI Literacy, Not a Computer Science Degree
item.description: Why lecturers need practical pedagogical, ethical and discipline-specific AI literacy to design curricula and assessment—without becoming programmers or IT experts.

item.title: Do Not Start with AI: Start with the Curriculum
item.description: A curriculum-design reflection on why educators should define graduate competence, human judgement and assessment evidence before deciding where AI belongs.

item.title: Waiting for Results: Reflections on Speaking to Hong Kong’s Future Physiotherapy Students
item.description: A reflection on speaking with students and families ahead of the HKDSE results, and on what admissions season reveals about anxiety, aspiration and the meaning of physiotherapy education in Hong Kong.

item.title: When Assessment Invites AI but Does Not Assess AI
item.description: A reflection on designing, questioning, and abandoning an AI-permitted assignment because AI use was not the intended learning outcome being assessed.

item.title: Beyond IQ: What Quotients Do Students Need in the AI Era?
item.description: A reflection on why students need adaptability, emotional intelligence, cultural awareness, social judgement, meaning and decency alongside cognitive ability.

item.title: Do Not Ask AI for the Answer First
item.description: A practical argument for using AI to ask probing questions after learners commit to an initial clinical judgement.

item.title: Using ChatGPT Is Not the Same as AI Literacy
item.description: A physiotherapy education reflection on why student exposure to ChatGPT does not automatically become safe, critical and professional AI use.

item.title: AI Can Draft Exam Questions, But It Cannot Validate Them
item.description: A reflection on why AI-generated assessment items still need expert review, blueprinting and validity evidence.

item.title: Two Years in Hong Kong: Reflecting on Teaching, Innovation, and Receiving a Teaching Excellence Award
item.description: A reflection on being nominated for a faculty teaching excellence award in 2025, receiving it in 2026, and what teaching, innovation and collaboration have meant during the first two years in Hong Kong.

item.title: When AI Makes Academia Faster, Who Gets the Time Back?
item.description: A reflection on academic acceleration, AI productivity, and why the new bottleneck is judgement rather than production.

item.title: Productive Struggle in the Age of AI
item.description: A reflection on whether students are learning inside too safe a bubble, and how AI can support or bypass productive struggle.

item.title: AI Policy Is Not Enough: Students Also Need Help Resisting the Pressure to Misuse AI
item.description: A reflection on why academic integrity responses to generative AI should address pressure, peer norms, misinformation and verification, not only detection.

item.title: AI Should Be a Thinking Partner, Not a Clinical Shortcut
item.description: An argument for teaching physiotherapy students to reason first, consult AI second, and remain accountable for clinical judgement.

item.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Using OpenClaw to Reclaim My Academic Life
item.description: A controlled exploration of whether agentic AI can reduce administrative workload while preserving privacy, professional judgement and academic accountability.

item.title: Reflections on a Teaching and Learning Conference
item.description: A reflection on moving the higher-education conversation about AI from novelty towards evidence, implementation and educational purpose.

item.title: A Tale of Two Graduations: From South Africa to Hong Kong
item.description: Reflections on graduation ceremonies in South Africa and Hong Kong, and the shared pride, sacrifice and hope that they represent.

item.title: The Weight of Decision: My Experience as a University Admissions Interviewer
item.description: An examination of fairness, bias and responsibility in university admissions interviews.

item.title: Supporting Students with Special Educational Needs: A Guide for Lecturers
item.description: Practical principles for removing barriers and creating an inclusive learning environment for students with special educational needs.

item.title: Responding to Student Mental Health Crises During Examinations
item.description: A practical guide to responding compassionately and safely to an acute student mental health crisis during an examination.

item.title: Navigating Virtual Reality: Comparing HTC VIVE, Meta Quest 2, Quest 3 and Quest Pro
item.description: An education-focused comparison of PC-based HTC VIVE systems, Meta Quest 2, Quest 3 and Quest Pro.

item.title: Embracing Wireless VR: A Guide to Setting Up a Meta VR Headset
item.description: A practical introduction to setting up a standalone Meta Quest headset safely and purposefully for teaching.

item.title: Setting Up VR: Reflections on the Experience
item.description: Reflections on the time, equipment and technical support required to set up an HTC VIVE Cosmos system.

item.title: Exploring 3D Organon in Virtual Reality
item.description: Initial reflections on 3D Organon and the educational questions that should guide evaluation of virtual anatomy tools.

item.title: What Do You Need to Succeed?
item.description: A playful word exercise prompts a wider reflection on knowledge, hard work, attitude and the many influences on success.

item.title: The Road to a PhD
item.description: A short reflection on doctoral supervision and the process of turning enthusiasm into feasible, rigorous research.
